evidence: Cic. Cat. 1.20: quōrum voluntātem tacitōrum perspicis (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Of a person who says nothing, and of things that make no sound; also, passively, unspoken, kept secret (tacitum tenēre, Cic. de Or. 3.64). To be silent is tacēre (see be quiet); silently, tacitē (see silence).
Of night, places and the moon; Cato’s lūna silēns is the new moon, when it gives no light.

evidence: Cic. post Red. 1.3: mūtum forum, ēlinguem cūriam (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Unable to speak, dumb; of places and times where no sound is heard, silent (see mute).

phrases.latin: quod bonī est, id tacitus taceās tūte tēcum et gaudeās
phrases.english: if it’s good news, keep it to yourself, say nothing, and be glad

phrases.latin: aut quam sīdera multa, cum tacet nox
phrases.english: or as many as the stars when the night is silent

phrases.latin: sine tē omnia mea mūta esse
phrases.english: that without you everything of mine is silent
